questions.text: Which of the following is the primary goal of a Root Cause Analysis (RCA) following a sentinel event?

options.a: To assign blame to the responsible staff member
options.b: To identify underlying system failures that contributed to the event
options.c: To document the event for legal purposes
options.d: To determine the financial cost of the adverse event

questions.explanation: RCA focuses on identifying systemic causes rather than individual blame, allowing organizations to make lasting improvements to prevent recurrence.

questions.text: A 'near miss' in patient safety terminology refers to:

options.a: An event that resulted in minor patient harm
options.b: An unsafe condition that has not yet caused harm
options.c: An event that was caught before reaching the patient
options.d: An event reported anonymously by staff

questions.explanation: A near miss (also called a close call) is an event that could have caused harm but was intercepted before reaching the patient. It is a valuable learning opportunity.

questions.text: The 'Swiss Cheese Model' of accident causation suggests that:

options.a: A single failure is always sufficient to cause a patient safety event
options.b: Safety errors only occur in ICU settings
options.c: Multiple layers of defenses each have gaps, and when gaps align an accident occurs
options.d: Human error is the primary cause of all medical accidents

questions.explanation: James Reason's Swiss Cheese Model illustrates how multiple defensive layers (policies, procedures, technology, humans) each have gaps. Accidents occur when the gaps in all layers align simultaneously.

questions.text: Which culture best supports patient safety reporting?

options.a: A blame culture where individuals are held accountable for every error
options.b: A just culture that distinguishes between human error, at-risk behavior, and reckless behavior
options.c: A no-fault culture where no individual is ever held accountable
options.d: A hierarchical culture where only managers report safety events

questions.explanation: A just culture balances accountability with learning. It encourages reporting by differentiating between inadvertent human error, at-risk choices, and reckless behavior, holding each appropriately accountable.

questions.text: A Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) is best described as:

options.a: A reactive tool used after a patient safety event has occurred
options.b: A proactive risk assessment tool that identifies potential failure points before harm occurs
options.c: A staff satisfaction survey focused on safety perceptions
options.d: A method for calculating the financial impact of medical errors

questions.explanation: FMEA is a proactive, systematic technique used to anticipate what could go wrong in a process, assess the likelihood and severity of failure, and implement preventive controls.
